learningObjectives: Link a TestSheet to a Template.
Link the TestSheet Values to the TestStep Values in the Template.
Use the Check Template and Jump to Schema functions.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Linking a TestSheet to a Template

elements.text: A Template alone can't run as a test — it needs the TestSheet to supply the specific data for each generated TestCase (like knowing what color and transmission to put in our car-blueprint analogy).

elements.title: Link the TestSheet
items: Select the TestSheet in the TestCaseDesign section, then drag and drop it onto the Template in the TestCase section.
Best practice: link a TestSheet to a Template as soon as it's created, to avoid confusion later about which Template relates to which TestSheet.

Each TestSheet should be linked to exactly ONE Template. If you need the same data in multiple Templates, use Classes (covered in Test Design Specialist Level 1) — do not link one TestSheet to several Templates.

elements.text: Jump to Schema Definition — once linked, a new ribbon option appears under the TestCase tab. Right-click the Template → Jump to Schema Definition (shortcut: Ctrl+J) to instantly navigate to its linked TestSheet. You can also confirm the linked TestSheet's name via the Property tab.
Linking the TestSheet doesn't automatically tell Tosca which TestStepValue uses which piece of data — you must link the individual Values.

elements.title: Link TestSheet Values to TestStepValues
items: Best practice: drag and drop each Value from the TestSheet onto the relevant TestStepValue in the TestCase.
Example: drag the Attribute 'Size' from the TestSheet onto the 'Size' TestStepValue — this automatically creates an XL reference.
The XL reference contains the path Tosca follows to find the value in the TestSheet at runtime.

elements.description: Right-click the Template → Check Template to validate that all XL references actually resolve to something in the TestSheet. Important: this ONLY checks that the links exist — it does NOT check for functionality errors in TestSteps or formulas. The function highlights the TestStepValue containing the broken link, not the XL reference text itself.

elements.text: Check Template validates reference EXISTENCE only. It will not catch a wrong formula, a bad Condition, or incorrect TestStep logic — those still need manual review or a test run to surface.

An XL reference can also be typed manually, using the syntax {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} or {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute.SubSubAttribute]} — but this is NOT best practice. Drag-and-drop is preferred since it avoids typos and guarantees the path actually matches the TestSheet's structure.

Once the Template is complete and its Workstate is set to COMPLETE, the next step is Instantiation — the process where Tosca creates actual TestCases based on the TestSheet (and any Conditions, covered in a later lesson).

elements.title: Instantiate
items: Select the Template → click Instantiate in the Ribbon's TestCase tab, OR
Right-click the Template → Create TemplateInstance from the Mini Toolbar, then confirm 'start instantiation now?', OR
Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.
The Template itself is unchanged; a new TemplateInstance folder appears below it containing the generated TestCases.
Run all TestCases in the Scratchbook to confirm they behave as expected.

elements.text: For our example, instantiation creates 4 TestCases — one per TestSheet Instance. Each generated TestCase shows only the steps/values relevant to it (e.g. the ValidValues TestCase uses the default size M; the Wrong-size TestCase uses the invalid XL) — Values from the TestSheet replace the References.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking Check Template catches all errors
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume a passed Check Template means the Template is fully correct.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check Template only validates that XL references resolve to something in the TestSheet — it does NOT check TestStep functionality, formulas, or logic errors.

examPitfalls.title: Linking one TestSheet to multiple Templates
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners reuse the same TestSheet across several Templates to save time.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Each TestSheet should link to exactly one Template. For shared data across multiple Templates, use Classes instead (Test Design Specialist Level 1 topic).

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting to check the linked TestSheet before troubleshooting
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates manually search for which TestSheet is linked to a Template.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Right-click the Template → Jump to Schema Definition (Ctrl+J) instantly navigates to the linked TestSheet; the Property tab also shows its name.

examPitfalls.title: Typing XL references manually instead of drag-and-drop
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates hand-type {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} paths to save a step, introducing typos that silently break the link.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: XL references CAN be typed manually with {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} syntax, but this is not best practice — drag-and-drop from the TestSheet is safer and guarantees the path is correct.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you link a TestSheet to a Template in Tosca?

options.text: TestSheets link automatically to the most recently created Template.
Right-click the Template and select 'Import TestSheet'.
Select the TestSheet in TestCaseDesign, then drag and drop it onto the Template in the TestCase section.
Copy the TestSheet's XML and paste it into the Template's properties.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a drag-and-drop action, same direction as most Tosca linking.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You select the TestSheet from TestCaseDesign and drag it onto the Template in the TestCase section to link them.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the Check Template function actually validate?

options.text: That all formulas used in Conditions produce the correct output.
That the ExecutionList linked to the Template is configured correctly.
That every TestStep will execute correctly against the live SUT.
That the XL references in the Template resolve to existing values in the linked TestSheet — nothing about TestStep functionality or formulas.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about reference existence, not runtime correctness.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Check Template only validates that XL references exist and resolve correctly in the linked TestSheet. It does not catch functionality errors in TestSteps or formulas — that's a common exam trap.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the shortcut to jump directly from a Template to its linked TestSheet?

options.text: Ctrl+J (Jump to Schema Definition).
Ctrl+T.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.

practiceQuiz.hint: Not the same shortcut as Instantiate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+J is the shortcut for 'Jump to Schema Definition', which navigates from the Template directly to its linked TestSheet. Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I is the Instantiate shortcut, not this one.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you link a value from the TestSheet to a specific TestStepValue in the Template?

options.text: Drag and drop the value from the TestSheet directly onto the TestStepValue — this creates an XL reference.
Type the value's name manually into the TestStepValue field.
XL references cannot be created manually; only Instantiate creates them.
Use the Check Template function to auto-link all values.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same drag-and-drop pattern as linking the TestSheet itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dragging and dropping a TestSheet value onto a TestStepValue creates an XL reference — the path Tosca follows at runtime to fetch the value from the TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE are valid ways to Instantiate a Template?

options.text: Right-click the Template → Create TemplateInstance from the Mini Toolbar.
Select the Template and use the shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.
Rename the Template to 'Instance_1'.
Select the Template, click Instantiate in the Ribbon's TestCase tab.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is a ribbon button, one is a context menu action, one is a keyboard shortcut.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Instantiation can be triggered via the Ribbon's Instantiate button, via right-click → Create TemplateInstance, or via the Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I shortcut. Renaming does nothing functionally. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: If the same test data is required across several different Templates, what should you use instead of linking one TestSheet to all of them?

options.text: Classes.
Multiple copies of the same TestSheet, pasted into each Template.
RequirementSets.
ExecutionLists.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is flagged in the course as a Test Design Specialist Level 1 topic.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tosca recommends using Classes when the same data is needed across multiple Templates, rather than linking one TestSheet to several Templates (which is harder to maintain).

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the manual syntax for typing an XL reference directly into a TestStepValue, and is it recommended?

options.text: $XL{Attribute::SubAttribute}$ — valid and equally recommended as drag-and-drop.
{XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} — valid, but not best practice compared to drag-and-drop.
There is no manual syntax; XL references can only ever be created by drag-and-drop.
{CP[Attribute.SubAttribute]} — the recommended and only supported method.

practiceQuiz.hint: Don't confuse this with the {CP[...]} syntax used for Test Configuration Parameters.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An XL reference can be typed manually as {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} or {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute.SubSubAttribute]}, but Tosca's official guidance flags this as NOT best practice — drag-and-drop from the TestSheet is safer and avoids typos.
